In this paper, taking SOFC system as the research object, a method of condition division and identification of SOFC system based on fusion clustering is proposed. Take the typical air leakage fault as the main body, use the fusion clustering algorithm to get the clustering tags under different operating conditions; then use the RBF-SVM classification algorithm to train the clustering tags, and get the working condition identification model. The results show that this method can effectively identify the working condition type of air leakage in SOFC system, and can be extended to the fault diagnosis of fuel leakage.

articleTitle: Analysis and promotion of multi-source ship shore power system based on prospect theory
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: In the context of energy saving and emission reduction and building green ports, ship-to-shore power technology is one of the important strategies favored by governments to solve port pollution. This paper describes the development background of marine shore power technology, introduces the composition and power supply mode of multi-source shore power system, analyzes the port multi-source ship shore power based on the prospect theory, the practical value and application prospects of multi-source marine shore power systems are described.

articleTitle: Cleaning and Reconstruction of Wind Power Anomaly Data based on Hierarchical Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of difficulty in identifying various types of abnormal operation data of wind turbines in wind farms and low reconstruction accuracy, this paper proposes a method of cleaning and reconstruction of abnormal wind power data based on hierarchical clustering. This method uses numerical information and dynamic time warping (DTW) methods to accurately capture data features, which can quickly and accurately identify various anomalies in the original data, and use the same metric to find the most simi-lar data in the dataset for data reconstruction. We compare this method with quartile-clustering algorithm, Copula function confidence interval model, and isolated forest algorithm. The results show that the method can quickly and effectively identify anomalous data and reconstruct them with high overall efficiency, and has some practical engineering value.

articleTitle: An improved genetic-backpropagation neural network for state of charge estimation of lithium-ion batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The state of charge estimation with high precision plays an important role in the usage of lithium-ion batteries in electronic vehicles. An improved genetic-backpropagation neural network (GA-BPNN) is proposed to predict the state of charge with high precision under complex working conditions. Specifically, the elite retention strategy is introduced to genetic operations to enhance the efficiency of the algorithm. Moreover, a further performance comparison of the improved GA-BPNN is achieved to prove its effectiveness. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the improved GA-BPNN is 7.92% and 6.71% under BBDST and DST working conditions, which are higher than that of traditional methods.

articleTitle: Research on Joint Optimization Configuration of Low Carbon Equipment in Comprehensive Energy System Based on Life Cycle Analysis Carbon Emissions and Carbon Trading
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The integrated energy system (IES) has the advantages of energy complementary coupling and multi-energy cascade utilization, and its rational allocation is conducive to improving economic and environmental benefits. Considering that IES also generates significant CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions during the production and construction of new energy equipment and energy storage equipment. Therefore, this paper analyzes based on the IES system with electricity gas heat load. Firstly, the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission model of last energy equipment and energy storage device is built by utilizing the life cycle analysis (LCA) method; Secondly, when considering the reasonable allocation of IES based on the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions of the whole life cycle, the excessive penalty mechanism of tiered carbon trading is incorporated; Finally, the new energy units and energy storage equipment are coordinated and optimized by taking IES energy purchase cost, construction cost, carbon emission cost, wind and light abandonment cost as multi-objective.

articleTitle: An Imitation Learning-based Approach for Power System Transient Stability Emergency Control
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The grid emergency control techniques are facing great challenge with the increasing complexity and uncertainty of modern power systems. To overcome this issue, this paper proposes an imitation learning-based approach for power systems transient stability emergency control. Proposed method can reasonably and effectively utilize the actual existing expert data to enhance the algorithm convergence and improve the control effect. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the efficiency and reliability of grid emergency control as well as reduces the manual intervention costs, thus showing great potential for practical application, providing valuable reference in maintaining security and stability of power systems.

articleTitle: Ultra-High Sensitivity Thin Film Heat Flux Sensor for Battery Thermal Runaway Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Thin-film heat flux sensor (HFS) can be widely used in the field of battery safety monitoring of new energy vehicles. In order to improve the accuracy of traditional engineering experience in the design of thin-film heat flux sensor and reduce the number of iterations, a finite element analysis model of thin-film heat flux sensor based on finite element simulation method is proposed in this paper. The model analyzes the effects of heat flux density and thermal resistance layer thickness on the temperature gradient of cold junction. At a heat flux density of 100 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the temperature difference is only 0.17 K, while at 1500 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, it reaches 2.53 K. The temperature difference on the lower surface of HFS membrane is positively related to the heat flux. When the thickness of the thermal resistance layer increases from 2 μm to 15 μm, the corresponding temperature difference also increased from 0.034 K to 0.251 K. In addition, there is a good linear relationship between the temperature difference and the thickness of the thermal resistance layer (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.99996), which shows that the performance of the thin film heat flux sensors is further optimised with the change of the thickness of the thermal resistance layer. This study provides a solid foundation for heat flux sensor and its application field of battery safety monitoring in new energy vehicles.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Solar Energy-Efficient Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: This comprehensive study delves deeply into the innovative integration of solar energy conservation systems with hydrogen storage and fuel cell power generation, specifically tailored for high-energy consumption environments like data centers. Recognizing the challenges posed by the intermittent nature of solar energy, the research underscores the pivotal role of such hybrid systems in ensuring a consistent and reliable power source. Through meticulous simulation and optimization processes, the study reveals that the strategic inclusion of batteries in the solar energy conservation system not only significantly reduces operational costs but also ensures a consistent and stable power supply to demanding loads. Furthermore, empirical data from the system's performance on a typical day provides compelling evidence of its capability to operate seamlessly and efficiently, strictly adhering to the pre-defined energy management strategy, thereby offering a promising solution for future energy demands.

articleTitle: Research on the development and detection technology of CAN interface chip suitable for relay protection devices
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Core chips of the secondary equipment in the power grid are very important to the stable operation of relay protection devices. It is necessary to conduct research on key technologies of industrial grade CAN interface chips to reduce the impact of chip power outage and ensure the safe and stable operation of the large power grid. This article analyzes the usage scenarios and application requirements of CAN interface chips in relay protection devices, compares the performance indicators of relevant chips in China and abroad, and proposes the technical indicators and key technologies for chip design of CAN interface chips suitable for relay protection devices. By studying the impact of core performance indicators of CAN interface chips on the performance of the entire device, a testing and inspection plan that takes into account the impact of CAN interface chips on the performance of the protection device is proposed, promoting the development of domestic chips, enhancing the independent controllability of chips, and ensuring the safe and reliable operation of the power grid.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis and Enhancement for BDFIG Based Virtual Synchronous Control
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The brushless doubly-fed induction generators (BDFIG) has a promising application prospect in wind power generation, owing to their durability, reliability and low maintenance cost. Implemented with virtual synchronous control (VSynC), the BDFIG-based wind turbines are capable of exhibiting inertial characteristics and providing frequency support to the power grid. However, when facing significant disturbances, the VSynC-based BDFIG may experience transient instability phenomenon. To solve this problem, the instability mechanism of the VSynC-based BDFIG is analyzed via the equal-area criterion. Then, the influence of key parameters on the transient stability of the system is explicitly clarified. Besides, an improved VSynC is proposed based on an expansive state observer to enhance the transient stability of BDFIG system. Finally, the accuracy of the theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of the proposed method have been validated through simulations.

articleTitle: An Improved Adaptive Velocity Update Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Parameter Identification of Lithium-ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The accuracy of SOC estimation is placed on its model establishment of Lithium-ion batteries. Aiming to enhance the precision accuracy for parameter identification of lithium-ion batteries’ equivalent circuit model (ECM), this article provides an improved adaptive velocity update PSO algorithm. Traditional PSO algorithm is frequently utilized for identifying the parameters of the ECM offline. However, the selection of control parameters affects the performance and effectiveness of this algorithm. Thus, this article proposes an adaptive velocity update formula according to the fitness value. Finally, compared with the simulation results obtained by using the Recursive Least Square (RLS) method and standard PSO algorithm for parameter identification, the results illustrate that the simulated terminal voltage errors are reduced by 85mV, and 13mV, respectively, which verifies that the improved parameter identification method has good accuracy.

articleTitle: Tuning Reserve Margins in Long Term Unit Commitment Integrated Generation Expansion Planning to Enhance Capacity Adequacy
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The reserve margin parameter within long-term Unit Commitment (UC) integrated Generation Expansion Planning (GEP) models plays a crucial role in meeting annual generation adequacy requirements. However, determining the reserve margin is generally conducted via rule-of-thumb methods. Inspired by our recent advancements in efficiently solving long-term UC integrated GEP models, this paper introduces a more scientifically-grounded trial-and-error approach for tuning the reserve margin parameters. This approach incrementally enhances the reserve margin. In each iteration, once the UC integrated GEP model is resolved, the tentative investment decisions are fed into a reliability assessment model to evaluate their probabilistic indicator—the Loss of Load Hours (LOLH). The assessment model accommodates hourly variations in wind, photovoltaic, and load by employing profiles of 8760-hour durations. This process continues until the LOLH complies with predefined standards. A case study based on the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) region substantiates that appropriate reserve margins can be determined to ensure the LOLH meets the reliability requirements annually.

articleTitle: Adaptability assessment method of AC/DC distribution network with high percentage of new energy sources
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: In line with advancements of the "double carbon" goal, the AC/DC distribution network incorporating a high proportion of new energy sources are expected to become the predominant form of future distribution system. Under the influence of source and load uncertainty, it is extremely important to accurately and quantitatively evaluate the adaptability of the distribution network. In this paper, considering the source and load uncertainty, we propose a method to evaluate the adapt-ability of AC/DC distribution network applicable to a high proportion of new energy sources from the aspects of flexibility and controllability. Firstly, the network flexibility assessment indexes of distribution network are established from the perspective of operation state. Then, the decoupling of AC/DC distribution network is partitioned, and the controllability indexes are constructed by considering the network topology and the adjustable power balance degree. Further-more, the network flexibility and controllability are assessed. Finally, the flexibility and controllability of pure AC and AC/DC distribution networks are evaluated in a city distribution network. The example shows that the hybrid AC/DC net-work structure has better adaptability.

articleTitle: A novel state-of-health prediction method based on Bi-directional Long Short-term memory network by Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The state-of-health (SOH) is a fundamental aspect of battery management systems (BMS). It describes the current aging status of the battery and is important for early warning of battery failure and thermal runaway. Accurate SOH estimation ensures battery safety and reliability. In this thesis, Discharge capacity data is used as input data for SOH estimation, and a SOH estimation method based on RW-GWO-BiLSTM for lithium-ion batteries is proposed in a data-driven framework. Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimization (RW-GWO) is an optimization method that improves Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) by introducing random walks to make the algorithm more flexible in searching the solution space to find the global optimal solution. Bi-directional Long Short-term Memory Network (BiLSTM) can effectively capture the temporal dependencies in sequence data, which helps to extract the hidden patterns and regularities in the discharge phase data. A comprehensive SOH estimation model was developed by combining RW-GWO with BiLSTM. The model was tested on diverse datasets and compared with existing models, highlighting the exceptional estimation performance and robustness of the method across various lithium-ion battery types, operational scenarios, and aging levels.

articleTitle: Simulation study of transient overvoltage at HVDC transmission terminal
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: This For high voltage DC transmission system, DC phase change failure shall cause transient overvoltage at the transmission side of the grid bus, and between the delivery system and the DC system the reactive power exchanged will change dramatically when the phase change fails. Therefore, we analyze the mechanism and characteristics of the transient overvoltage at the AC bus at the transmission end after the phase change failure caused by the AC fault on the receiving end, and build a system model of positive and negative 800KV high-voltage DC transmission Using the PSCAD-EMTDC simulation platform, an analysis is conducted to examine the transient overvoltage and reactive power variations at the transmitter bus during different AC faults. Additionally, the transient behavior of the DC system voltage and current is studied. Through adjusting and optimizing the parameters of the fixed control system. Obtained through simulation that when Phase change fault occurs, the transient characteristics of the sending bus voltage exhibit a decreasing trend followed by an increase. During a phase change failure, the reactive power flow between the receiving system and the DC system is reversed. The DC system acts as a reactive power absorber, drawing in a considerable amount of reactive power from the sending system. Subsequently, it releases a substantial imaginary power back into the sending system.

articleTitle: Key Node Selection and Network Simplification Method for Distribution Network with High Penetration of Distributed Photovoltaics
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: In view of modeling complexity and difficulties in online power flow analysis for the large-scale medium and low voltage distribution network (DN), this paper proposes a key node selection and network simplification method for DN with high penetration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs). The proposed approach can reduce the dependence of online power flow analysis on comprehensive measurement of the entire system and can increase the efficiency of power flow calculation by breaking down the large-scale complex DN into a small-scale equivalent network. Firstly, the network is partitioned into various regions with nodes that have similar amplitudes of voltage using the K-means algorithm and the similarity index of peak and valley voltage values. On the basis of the network partition, the nodes with peak and valley voltage in each region are selected as the key nodes of DN, together with the controllable PV nodes. Then, network simplification meth-od based on the node voltage equation is proposed to convert the original complicated DN model into a simplified network model in accordance with the online measurement data of important nodes. Finally, an adjusted IEEE 123-node case is used to verify the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A node importance evaluation method based on Monte Carlo simulation and VIKOR for grids containing new energy
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Due to the deep coupling between the power and cyber networks and the un-certainty of new energy, the security issues of modern power grids, as a typical cyber-physical system, are becoming increasingly prominent. The node importance evaluation of power grids plays a crucial role in ensuring its reliability and security. This paper proposes a comprehensive node importance evaluation scheme by CRITIC and VIKOR methods. Monte Carlo simulation is used to handle the uncertainty of wind power generation, and a node importance index (GLT) is proposed considering the generation, load, and transmission capacity of the nodes in the power grid. A decision matrix containing the GLT and the other five evaluation indexes is constructed from two aspects of electrical and topology characteristics, and the CRITIC and VIKOR methods are used to integrate the indexes of the decision matrix into a comprehensive importance evaluation index. In the simulation tests, the metrics of power supply and survival node rate are adopted to verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method, which can effectively identify the critical nodes in the power grid.

articleTitle: Temperature simulation and analysis of power battery module with PCM
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: In order to explore the influence of convective heat transfer coefficient and phase change material (PCM) on battery module temperature, the heat generation model of battery and heat transfer model of PCM was established, and ANSYS fluent was used to simulate the temperature distribution of the battery module, whose maximum temperature, maximum temperature difference and liquid fraction were used to study the battery module’s heat dissipation performance. The results show that with the increase of convective heat transfer coefficient, the maximum temperature of the module almost tends to be stable, but the temperature difference will increase. In addition, different PCMs will affect its maximum temperature difference.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Energy System Considering Demand Response of Multiple Controllable Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: To optimize the total operating cost of an integrated energy system (IES), an IES optimal scheduling model is proposed based on the demand response of multiple controllable loads. The model takes into consideration the commodity attributes of natural gas and power energy on the demand side. Two DR models are developed using the peak-valley price strategy for different loads. These models include the power-gas DR model, which utilizes a price elasticity matrix, and the alternative DR model that considers energy conversion. Furthermore, a heat-cooling load model is established, considering the fuzziness in human body's temperature perception. Finally, an optimal scheduling model is constructed, which minimizes the total cost by considering the energy purchase cost, equipment operation and maintenance cost, and DR compensation cost. The model is solved using the CPLEX solver. Simulation analysis with multiple scenarios demonstrates the cost reduction effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: A kind of variable pitch control of wind turbine based on fuzzy control under extreme wind conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The classical PID controller is widely used in engineering, but in the face of abrupt extreme wind conditions, the constant PID controller parameters can not control the pitch Angle in time, resulting in great changes in the speed, even beyond the limit. In order to further control the speed change of wind turbine under extreme wind conditions, this paper proposes to introduce fuzzy control into the segmented PID controller. By taking the speed difference and the speed change rate as input, the fuzzy controller can determine the change of PID controller parameters in advance, and then realize the advance operation of the wind turbine variable speed system. Finally, the control of speed overrun is realized. In this paper, a 5MW fan model is built on MATLAB/Simulink for simulation. The results show that the method proposed in this paper can realize the advance action of pitch Angle under extreme wind conditions and effectively control the change of speed.

articleTitle: Microgrid-Distribution Network Bi-layer Economic Optimal Dispatch Considering Source-network-load-storage Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The uncertainty and volatility of distributed generation (DG) will significantly influence on the grid-connected operation of microgrid, leading to a lack of sufficient utilization of renewable energy. In response to this issue, this article establishes a two-layer collaborative economic optimization scheduling model for microgrid distribution networks that considers grid load storage. The upper layer model takes the highest profit of the distribution network in the context of an open distribution network as the optimization objective, and uses an enhanced adaptive differential evolution algorithm to solve it. At the lower level, the model considers multiple adjustable units. It aims to optimize the total cost of microgrids. Finally, the simulation results indicate that by effectively scheduling controllable resources in the network, microgrids can effectively reduce operating costs and play an important role in "peak shaving". By exchanging electricity with the distribution network, not only does it improve the economic benefits of microgrids and distribution networks, but it also reduces the occurrence of waste renewable energy and improves the utilization capacity of renewable resources.

articleTitle: A Deep-Reinforcement-Learning-based Optimal Scheduling for Rural Integrated Energy System Considering the Uncertainties of Renewable Energies and Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The optimal scheduling of rural integrated energy system (RIES) confronts significant challenges owing to the uncertainties of renewable energies and power loads as well as the diverse kinds of penetrated energies. To this end, a novel approach based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is proposed to achieve the excellent performances of economy, environmental friendliness and reliability without loss of robustness of RIES. The key idea is to adaptively and immediately coordinates all the energies outputs with the uncertainties of the renewable energy sources and loads of RIES by means of DDPG, where the change process of the renewable energies and loads can be in fact treated as Markov Decision Process (MDP) and this forms a steady-state control problem. By means of the DDPG algorithm that interacting the RIES environment, the optimal scheduling policy of the RIES considering uncertainty of renewable energies and loads can be adaptively achieved with a fast response. The comparisons in various scenarios verify the advantages of the proposed approach in terms of reducing operation cost and carbon dioxide emission while enhancing the energy supply reliability of RIES without loss of robustness and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimized High Energy Vibration Environmental for Four-way Joint Lock Nut of Hydraulic Pipeline in Aircraft Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: During ground inspection of aircraft hydraulic system, it is found that the lock nut on four-way joint of hydraulic system is loose and the fuse is broken, which will seriously affect normal aircraft operation of energy storage equipment. To grasp the loosening mechanism of four-way locking nut joint of the energy storage device hydraulic pipeline to ensure safe flight, this paper proposes a comprehensive failure analysis of lock nut and fuse for aircraft energy storage systems. In addition, designing a specialized fixture that can withstand high vibration environments to cleverly combine the hydraulic pipeline, four-way joint, locking nut, and other components into actual aircraft installation state. Taking high energy vibration load spectrum of aircraft engine compartment as input vibration excitation condition, the multidirectional ground vibration test is carried out, and the phenomenon of aircraft energy storage systems hydraulic pipeline four-way joint locking nut loosening is reproduced. The experiment found that under continuous high energy vibration environment, the locking nut and anti-corrosion tape continue to wear and produce gaps, which exacerbate the lock nut failure. When the lock nut is rotated 15° clockwise, the preload completely fails and fuse cannot play a protective role in whole process. When lock nut reaches the limit counterclockwise, it is pulled by fuse and hits fuse contact point and safety hole, and fuse continues to wear or even fail. The experimental results show the root cause of four-way joint loose locking nut of hydraulic pipeline, and provide guidance for the safe energy storage and installation process of the aircraft energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Real time operation data mining algorithm for power systems based on adaptive incremental clustering algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: There are complex correlation relationships and interactive effects between various components and parameters in the power system. Therefore, how to accurately mine these association relationships from real-time data and establish accurate models to describe and predict power system behavior is a challenging task. To improve the safety of the power system, optimize operational efficiency, improve maintenance and management, and support the development of intelligent power systems. A real-time operation data mining algorithm for power systems based on adaptive incremental clustering algorithm has been proposed. Using wavelet packet method to denoise real-time operation data of power system and remove noise from real-time operation data of power system. Using principal component analysis to extract real-time operational data features of power systems. On this basis, based on the adaptive incremental clustering algorithm, the extracted real-time operational data features of the energy system can be explored through adaptive incremental clustering. The experimental results show that this algorithm has high accuracy in real-time data mining of energy systems and can effectively reduce the real-time running time of energy systems.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis And Mechanism Identification Approach for Micro-short of Power Lithium Iron Phosphate Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: With the rapid development of power lithium-ion battery industry in recent years, its safety performance has gradually attracted widespread attention. This paper reports our research on micro-short fault of power lithium iron phosphate battery. Two different experiments which might induce micro-short were designed. According to the experiment results and external features of micro-short fault, a diagnostic approach based on module redundancy was proposed, which obtained the voltage correlation coefficient in serial module and temperature residual in parallel module to detect and locate the individual cell suffering micro-short in the module. Then the mechanism of micro-short fault was identified through variation tendency of incremental capacity curves. Post-mortem examination was carried out to validate the effectiveness of the proposed fault diagnosis and mechanism identification approach.

articleTitle: Research on energy hub selection and capacity planning considering demand response uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The Integrated Energy System (IES) enhances the utilization of renewable energy and the efficient use of terminal energy by employing multiple energy sources such as electricity, gas, cold, and heat. The development of the IES towards a low-carbon and sustainable direction relies on the integration of wind power generation and Demand Response (DR). However, the challenges arise from the fluctuation of wind power output and the uncertainty of demand response in the planning and operation of the IES. This thesis focuses on addressing the planning problem of the IES under the uncertainty of wind power and demand response. It conducts a comprehensive study on the planning, considering the uncertainty of demand response and wind power. The research primarily covers energy hub selection and capacity planning, considering demand response uncertainty. To minimize total costs of investment, operation, wind curtailment, and demand response, a model is established. This model also takes into account energy balance constraints, equipment constraints within the energy hub, and power interaction constraints with the upper-level grid. The Gurobi solver is employed to solve the model. The case study results demonstrate that demand response can optimize energy hub configuration, promote wind power resource consumption, and enhance the economic efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Load Forecasting Model Considering Users’ Travel Rules
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The proportion of EV in total number of motor vehicles in China has increased rapidly. Under this background, it is of great significance to predict the EV charging load reasonably and accurately. By studying the travel rules of car used by personal objective, the EV charging load prediction is carried out. According to the user 's travel statistics, travel laws of EV are analyzed by the combination of user travel chain and Markov process (MP). Moreover, the charging load forecasting model is established under the two conditions which including EV charging at home and EV charging on the way. Finally, the Monte Carlo (MC) simulation method which used widely is adopted to calculate the charging load. In addition to this, the EV charging load distribution at different times and different regions is obtained. The simulation results in the software show that the established forecasting model can make accurate and reasonable predictions of charging loads for a large number of randomly dispersed electric private car.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Energy Storage Fluctuation Suppression Based on PI Control
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the development of a wind storage microgrid system utilizing hybrid energy storage. The objective is to contribute to the energy transformation and realization of the "dual carbon" goal. By implementing an intelligent power distribution control technique, the suggested system successfully harnesses the complementing qualities of batteries and super-capacitors while maximizing the power output of the wind power system. The response characteristics of the microgrid system are analyzed under three different operating conditions: off-grid, grid-connected, and grid-connected switching. The study aims to achieve smooth wind power fluctuations and ensure reliable load supply stability, guaranteeing the reliability of grid connection. In this work, a wind storage microgrid system model based on hybrid energy storage is established by using MATLAB/Simulink. To verify the effectiveness of the suggested control strategy under various operating situations, numerous simulations are run. The outcomes show that the system can maintain the stability of load power supply, smooth variations of wind power, and ensure the reliability of grid connection.

articleTitle: Internal Temperature Estimation of Power Lithium Batteries Based on GA-EKF Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Accurate estimation of internal battery temperature is vital for the secure functioning of power batteries. In order to obtain real-time and precise internal battery temperature, A technique for estimating the internal temperature of lithium-ion batteries is put forward, based on a combination of genetic optimization algorithm and extended Kalman filter algorithm. By combining the Bernardi battery heat generation model with the thermal circuit model, an equivalent thermal model for lithium-ion batteries is formulated. The correlation between internal and external temperatures of the battery is determined using the state equation analysis method. The genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to identify the parameters of the thermal model and validate the model accuracy. The estimation of internal battery temperature is achieved by integrating the GA algorithm with the extended Kalman filter (EKF) algorithm. Experimental trials performed on power batteries featuring embedded temperature sensors illustrate the efficacy of the proposed approach in accurately estimating the internal temperature of lithium-ion power batteries. with an estimation error of less than 1°C. This method provides a robust guarantee for real-time safety monitoring of power batteries.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Reconstruction Strategy with Demand-Side Response Incorporating Energy Storage and Flexible Multi-State Switches
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Building upon the intelligent and flexible multi-state switch distribution net-work reconstruction optimization model, this study considers the energy storage model and price-based demand response model, proposing a joint optimization strategy involving price-based demand response and intelligent energy storage with flexible multi-state switches in the distribution network. The user satisfaction model is constructed by multiplying the voltage deviation and investment cost variation, integrating user satisfaction, distribution network loss cost, and State of Operation (SOP) utilization cost as the combined optimization objectives. The Pareto frontier is employed to select the optimal solution set, and a comparative analysis of results from different scenarios is conducted to validate the superiority of this approach. The pro-posed strategy aims to enhance the adaptability and efficiency of the distribution network by incorporating demand-side response mechanisms and intelligent energy storage with multi-state switches. Through this optimization framework, the distribution network can effectively respond to changes in electricity demand, improve operational flexibility, and enhance overall efficiency. The study demonstrates that the joint optimization strategy provides significant improvements in user satisfaction, reduction of distribution net-work loss cost, and SOP utilization cost. Furthermore, it facilitates the integration of renewable energy sources, laying a solid foundation for the future development of intelligent and sustainable distribution networks.

articleTitle: Stability Estimation and Enhanced Control of BDFIG-Driven Wind Turbines under Weak Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The interaction between the weak grid impedance and grid-connected wind turbines (WTs) may lead to instability issue. Particularly, the stability of the brushless doubly-fed induction generators (BDFIGs)-based WTs under weak grid has not been fully estimated. To settle such problem, this paper develops a single-input single-output (SISO) model of the BDFIG system. Then, derived from stability analysis, a linear active disturbance rejection controller (LADRC)-based control strategy is proposed to enhance the system stability. The effects of key factors such as LADRC bandwidth and grid impedance on stability are evaluated comprehensively. Finally, the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Coordinated Restoration Strategy for Extreme Events in Traffic and Power Distribution Networks Considering Road Traffic Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: With the increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) in urban areas and the tight coupling between power distribution and traffic networks, there is a significant potential to enhance the resilience of urban infrastructure and expedite the recovery process during extreme events. In light of this, this paper proposes a coordinated recovery strategy for traffic and power distribution networks, based on a cellular transport model framework. Firstly, the impact of the recovery of coupled hubs on road traffic flow is analyzed, followed by an investigation into its influence on the restoration speed of important loads in the power distribution network. Subsequently, a coordinated recovery model is presented, where the scheduling of EVs, taking into account the objective of maximizing load recovery and minimizing dispatch costs, serves as the decision variable. This model aims to address the challenge of improving the efficiency of power and transportation system recovery during the short-term restoration period. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the strategy in enhancing the resilience of the power distribution network during extreme events.

articleTitle: SOC Balancing Control Strategy Based on Improved Adaptive Current Distribution Coefficient Algorithm for Multi-energy Storage Units in DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The DC microgrid has the advantages of simple internal structure, flexible control and no power quality issues related to frequency or reactive power. In an independent operation mode, energy storage units are required to maintain power stability of the system. However, multiple energy storage units are operated in parallel. It will have inconsistent state of charge (SOC) problem due to unreasonable power distribution. To achieve SOC fast balancing be-tween different energy storage units, an improved adaptive current distribution coefficient algorithm is proposed in this paper. The current distribution coefficient of the energy storage unit is dynamically adjusted by establishing a relationship between the coefficient and SOC through an exponential function, and the current of each battery group is continuously compared with the rated current. When the current of one group of batteries exceeds the rated current, it charges or discharges at the rated current while the other group supplies or absorbs the remaining current. When the current of both groups of batteries is less than the rated current, the current is distributed according to the current distribution coefficient. Compared with conventional adaptive current distributed control, the proposed algorithm improves the rapidity of SOC balance. Finally, simulation is conducted to verify the correctness of the proposed control strategy.

Author Keywords: Improved adaptive current distribution coefficient algorithm

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Storage Controller Parameters to Suppress Low-frequency Oscillation of High-proportion Wind-solar Access System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: To offer a comprehensive understanding of the role energy storage devices play in mitigating the system's low-frequency oscillations, the study delves into a high-proportion wind-solar grid-connected system of four machines and two regions. A mathematical model outlining the battery energy storage controller parameters is constructed and time-domain simulations are performed on the platform. Utilizing the eigenvalue analysis method, the eigenvalues and damping ratios provide a theoretical basis for quantitatively analyzing the optimization of energy storage controller parameters. To enhance the damping effect of the energy storage device, this paper introduces an Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) for optimizing the parameters across each link of the energy storage damping controller. The IPSO algorithm optimizes parameters by aiming for the minimal Integrated Time and Absolute Error (ITAE) index of the multi-controller. Simulation results reveal that the optimized energy storage device has markedly amplified the suppression of the system's low-frequency oscillation, thus significantly improving system stability.

articleTitle: Virtual Synchronous Generator Control Strategy Based on Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: AC microgrid, as an effective form of integrating new energy into the grid, has received more and more attention because of its unique advantages. In order to improve the inertia and damping of the AC microgrid and realize the friendly integration of new energy to the grid, a virtual synchronous genera-tor (VSG) control strategy applicable to the matrix converter is proposed. Aiming at the problem that the frequency of the traditional VSG cannot be restored to the rated value after the load power fluctuations, the VSG secondary frequency modulation control strategy is introduced. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the control strategy are verified in the island and grid-connected operation modes.

articleTitle: Dynamic Equivalence Modeling of Wind-thermal-bundled Power Transmission Through VSC-HVDC System Based on Trajectory Piecewise Linearization
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The wind-thermal-bundled power transmission through DC is a high-order nonlinear system, which has the disturbance caused by the variable operation mode and the uncertainty of wind power generation. Establishing a full-order model to describe the motion process after the disturbance is necessary. However, the simulation speed of the full-order model is slow, and it is not easy to design the controller. Therefore, a global linearization modeling method is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the full-order electromagnetic transient model of DFIG and VSC-HVDC is established in the DQ reference frame, and SRF-PLL connects the whole system. Then, three operating modes and two typical perturbations of the system are set, and Matlab/Simulink obtains the trajectory of disturbed motion. Furthermore, the Trajectory Piecewise Linearization (TPWL) method is used to establish a dynamic equivalence model of the wind-thermal-bundled power transmission via DC, including critical operating point selection, linearization, reduction, weight calculation, and Simulink verifies it. The results show that the dynamic equivalence model is highly consistent with the electromagnetic transient model after perturbation under the appropriate sampling point rate, which verifies the correctness of the global linearization modeling method.

articleTitle: A High-Precision SOC Estimation Method for Lithium-ion Batteries Based on Induced Ordered Weighted Averaging Operator Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Any single prediction model has its own defects and shortcomings, through the effective combining of single prediction models to form a combination of prediction models can effectively improve the prediction effect [1], [2]. In this paper, a combined prediction model for SOC estimation of lithium-ion batteries based on BP neural network model and LSTM neural network model is established by introducing the induced ordered weighted averaging operator (IOWA) algorithm, and charging and discharging data of lithium-ion batteries under different working conditions are selected to test the prediction performance of the combined prediction model. The experimental results show that the combined prediction model established in this paper effectively makes up for the prediction defects of the single prediction model, and has high prediction accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Research on the Short-Circuit Current of MMC-HVDC under DC Pole-to-pole Fault Considering the Impacts of DFIG
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Integrating a doubly-fed wind farm into the grid through high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission using a modular multilevel converter (MMC) is a common approach for wind power integration. During DC pole-to-pole faults in MMC-HVDC, the terminal voltage of the doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) symmetrically drops and triggers low voltage ride-through (LVRT) control to provide reactive power. However, due to different control methods between DFIG converter and MMC, there exists significant interaction between their transient processes. While previous research has focused on fault characteristics of MMC under pole-to-pole faults, the influences of DFIG have been excluded. This paper analyzes the timing characteristics of both MMC blocking and DFIG LVRT control, establishes fault equivalent circuits for DFIG and MMC-HVDC before and after MMC blocking, deduces short-circuit current expressions for MMC considering the impacts of DFIG under pole-to-pole faults, and analyzes both the influences of DFIG as well as characteristics of short-circuit currents in MMC. The proposed theoretical analysis was verified by PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Monitoring method of photovoltaic panel parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Photovoltaic energy as a clean and renewable energy, its large-scale development and utilization has been widely concerned by various countries in the world, the analysis of photovoltaic cell circuit model and parameter characteristics is an important content to judge the working state of photovoltaic panels. This paper conducted a study of photovoltaic panels, circuit model and parameters, according to different accuracy requirement, and proposes corresponding photovoltaic cell circuit model, when the external environmental factors change and quantitative analysis, the parameters of the photovoltaic cells will be how to change, which affect the output of the photovoltaic system.

articleTitle: Early Anomaly Detection of Power Battery Based on Time-series Features
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Early anomaly detection in power batteries is crucial to ensure safe and reliable operation of electric vehicles. Although a lot of research has been conducted on battery anomaly detection, little attention has been paid to the time-series features of the charging curves of single batteries. This paper proposes a power battery early anomaly detection method based on time-series features. By dynamically matching the charging segments with the historical charging data, seven different multi-timescale timing features are extracted, and the local outlier factor (LOF) algorithm is used to achieve the anomaly detection of a single unit. The experimental results show that the method can accurately detect abnormal cells in the battery pack before the warning of the battery management system by using only two of the features, and the false detection rate is less than 3%.

articleTitle: Hydro-Pump/Generator-based Hydrogen-Pressure Energy Storage for Power Grid-Forming Support
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: This paper presents a method to design water-compressed hydrogen energy storage system (WCH-ESS) and its active regulation function for the power grid. First, it proposed the system architecture of water-compressed hydrogen ESS station. Then, the station operation depends on the variable-speed constant frequency (VSCF) motor/generator as the core function. With the station and core function, the design method of active support function of power grid based on the WCH-ESS is proposed. Finally, the layout, function and risk avoidance design of the WCH-ESS based on an energy island is analyzed. This method can take the discarded wind/photovoltaic energy as the surplus electric energy to drive the motor to compress the hydrogen when the load of the power grid is low. For high-value electric energy, the system adopts the WCH-ESS to generate more power, which can participate in the frequency regulation of power grid to stabilize the power system. It can also be used as emergency backup to improve the consumption rate of wind power and photovoltaic power generation.

articleTitle: Aging path analysis of batteries under different energy storage operating conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The aging performance of energy storage battery in different stress and operating conditions is different, this paper takes 60A·h lithium-ion battery as the research object, and compares and studies the battery's decline aging path in the energy storage operating conditions under multiple stress combinations, respectively, in the energy storage tracking, frequency modulation(FM) and peaking, etc. under different single and combination conditions for cycling, the results show that: the battery declines more obviously in frequency modulation conditions in different single conditions; Combination of conditions, can improve the battery aging trend, extend the number of cycles of the battery, but the battery performance will be affected by different stress combinations; by comparing the pattern of change of the aging path of the battery under different operating conditions, it provides a basis for the operation strategy of the energy storage battery.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Distribution Line Based on Noise Adaptive Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Algorithm for three-phase line parameter identification based on noise adaptive Kalman filtering is proposed to address the problem of large deviation between measurement data and true values due to factors such as equipment aging and line interference, which affects the accuracy of parameter identification based on measurement data. Firstly, a state equation and a measurement equation for noise adaptive Kalman filtering are established based on the three-phase line model of the distribution system considering the coupled impedance. Then, an adaptive correction method for noise is introduced to continuously update the covariance matrix of measurement noise based on the residuals (i.e., the difference between the measured values and the predicted values), reducing the interference caused by the error in the covariance matrix of measurement noise and improving the accuracy of parameter identification results. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through case analysis results. Compared to traditional Kalman filtering methods, the proposed method in this paper achieves higher identification accuracy.

articleTitle: Cost Analysis of Multi-scenario Shared Energy Storage Considering Operational Life Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The synergistic implementation of shared energy storage across varied scenarios holds profound implications for optimizing energy storage's economic returns and fortifying the power grid's agility and robustness. Addressing this, our study introduces a nuanced cost-evaluation technique for shared energy storage facilities, rooted in representative operational life-cycle considerations. Leveraging a variable significance assessment approach, we pinpoint pivotal operational features and sketch out a lifespan distribution space for shared energy storage within multiple contexts. Prioritizing the per-kilowatt-hour investment cost of the storage infrastructure as our chief optimization target, we embark on an exhaustive life-cycle cost exploration across these scenarios. Case study results affirm that when the degradation rate during operations is accounted for, a more detailed perspective on the per-kilowatt-hour investment dynamics emerges, thus enhancing the granularity and accuracy of our economic assessments.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Flywheel Energy Storage Machine-Side Converter based on Three Vector Model Predictive Torque Control
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: The use of Flywheel Energy Storage Systems (FESS) has become increasingly popular, prompting extensive research into its control technology. In the regard, a research focus has emerged on the application of the three-vector model predictive torque control (MPTC) and the development of a power and torque double closed-loop control strategy for FESS. The output power response speed and steady-state power pulsation of FESS under power regulation control are aimed to be improved by utilizing a control structure based on direct power closed-loop control, instead of the traditional speed regulation control. Additionally, the conventional direct torque control (DTC) is also replaced with the three-vector model predictive torque control (TV-MPTC). To enhance the stability of the control system and reduce processor calculation time, a selection table for suboptimal voltage vector selection is introduced in the machine-side converter of FESS. Simulation results are presented for the two primary operating conditions of FESS, which demonstrate the favorable steady-state performance and transient performance of the proposed power control strategy.

Author Keywords: Three vector Model predictive torque control

articleTitle: Operation Strategy and Economic Analysis of Active Peak Regulation "Photovoltaic + Energy Storage" Power Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd New Energy and Energy Storage System Control Summit Forum (NEESSC)
abstract: Constructing a new type of power system primarily based on new energy is an essential pathway for the energy and power industry to achieve the "dual carbon" goals. To facilitate high proportions of new energy consumption and ensure the safe and stable operation of the grid, various provinces and cities have successively introduced policies requiring the configuration of a specific scale of energy storage in newly built new energy power stations. Building upon the analysis of the role of configuration of energy storage on the new energy side, this paper proposes an operational mode for active peak regulation "photovoltaic + energy storage" power stations, which can conduct active peak shaving and valley filling based on the characteristics of the grid load. An analysis of energy storage capacity configuration for "photovoltaic + energy storage" power stations under different depths of peak regulation is presented. This paper also exploratively and innovatively proposes an economically feasible method for calculating the benefits of "photovoltaic + energy storage", offering a novel approach to address the unsatisfactory economic returns for such power stations.
